newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end higher, feeder cattle mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end higher, feeder cattle mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed Tuesday's lightly traded session slightly higher amid talk cash cattle will trade up $1.00 next week at $66.00.
Feeder cattle closed mixed, with January down slightly partially in reaction to late gains in CBOT corn futures.
In live cattle, futures traded both sides of unchanged early but then held gains on the strength of buying by commission house Rand Financial.
Cash markets were quiet with meat packers bidding a steady $65.00 per cwt, while sellers passed those bids pricing cattle at $67.00.
Many meat packing plants were closed Tuesday, minimizing demand for cattle, traders said. USDA reported Tuesday's slaughter at 48,000 head versus 128,000 a week ago and 122,000 a year ago.

Feeder cattle futures closed narrowly mixed after trading both sides of unchanged throughout the session. Late gains in CBOT corn futures prompted light selling in January feeders to turn that contract lower.
The latest CME feeder index was up 0.17 cent at 65.56 cents per lb.
The CME livestock markets closed early at 1200 CST/1800GMT Tuesday in observance of Christmas and will be closed Wednesday.
Live cattle closed up 0.225 to 0.100 cent with February up 0.150 at 64.950. Feeder cattle were up 0.100 to down 0.100 cent with January off 0.075 at 67.350.
